core_insight.source_excerpt: narma is an "Enterprise Agentic Brain" designed for AI-first companies to see, prove, and deploy AI automation at scale. The architecture has three layers. Observe (Layer 1): lightweight desktop sensors capture work patterns including application usage, activity sequences, and time allocation. Intelligence Layer (Layer 2): a "Brain" that detects employee intent, the business value of tasks, and "drift" where work diverges from the intended flow. Execution Layer (Layer 3): an "Agent Factory" that automatically generates, deploys, and monitors AI agents for validated high-ROI opportunities with built-in approval gates. The system uses existing foundation models rather than building its own LLMs, focusing instead on the "Work Graph" to reveal where resources are burned and where AI can intercept work mid-flow to provide assistance. Vision: a single system that observes how work happens, decides what AI should not do next, and auto-builds agents continuously to ensure a "Continuous AI lift."
core_insight.if_wrong: If the system cannot accurately detect employee intent, identify high-ROI opportunities, or effectively deploy autonomous agents, then AI-first companies will continue to struggle with AI adoption, and narma's value proposition will be undermined.
core_insight.why_different: Narma focuses on a holistic, continuous observation and autonomous agent deployment system, contrasting with potentially fragmented or manually intensive existing AI deployment strategies.

raw.thesis: Narma proposes an "Enterprise Agentic Brain" for AI-first companies to scale AI automation. The core innovation lies in its three-layered architecture: an "Observe" layer with desktop sensors to capture work patterns, an "Intelligence Layer" that interprets employee intent and identifies "drift" in workflows, and an "Execution Layer" or "Agent Factory" that autonomously generates and deploys AI agents for high-ROI opportunities. This system aims to provide "Continuous AI lift" by leveraging existing foundation models and focusing on the "Work Graph" to optimize resource allocation and inject AI assistance mid-workflow. Narma positions itself as a solution for AI-first companies struggling with unquantifiable AI savings, unreliable ROI measurements, and workflow inconsistencies. It replaces existing, fragmented approaches to AI deployment and monitoring within large enterprises by offering a unified, intelligent system. The founder is building a growth-oriented startup given the emphasis on "scale" and "Continuous AI lift" within AI-first companies. The venture is currently at the idea stage, as evidenced by the detailed architectural description without mention of any built product or user traction. The venture aims to solve the problem of identifying and demonstrating the tangible business value of AI automation, a significant challenge for enterprises investing in AI.
raw.core_excitement: The founder is excited by the vision of a single, intelligent system that can observe how work happens, decide what AI should do, and continuously build agents to ensure "Continuous AI lift" for AI-first companies.
raw.what_makes_this_different: Narma's distinction lies in its comprehensive, three-layered "Enterprise Agentic Brain" that observes work patterns, infers intent, and autonomously deploys AI agents for continuous, measurable AI lift, rather than relying on fragmented or manual AI integration methods.

market_data.why_better: Narma provides a single system to observe work, decide AI actions, and auto-build agents continuously for 'Continuous AI lift,' addressing the challenges of unquantifiable savings, unreliable ROI, and workflow drift.
market_data.trigger_now: Struggle with lack of telemetry to pinpoint AI savings, unreliable ROI measurements, and constant drift in systems and human resources within AI-first companies desiring to scale AI automation.
market_data.buyer: AI-first companies, potentially leadership or operations departments responsible for AI strategy and deployment.
market_data.end_user: Employees within AI-first companies whose work patterns and workflows are being observed and automated.
market_data.alternatives: Fragmented or manual approaches to AI deployment and monitoring; lack of telemetry; unreliable ROI measurements; existing systems that struggle with drift.

things_that_must_work: Accurate detection of employee intent and business value of tasks
Effective and reliable autonomous generation and deployment of AI agents
Seamless integration with existing foundation models and enterprise models
Enterprise-grade approval gates for AI agent deployment
